messages:
Maria: Heads-up — support received multiple reports of elevated p95/p99 for the hosted API from APAC customers starting ~09:10UTC. Symptoms: TLS handshake stalls and ~2-3s extra connection setup before tokens stream.
Ajay: Are these new clients or existing traffic? Any correlation with specific regions or model routes?
Support Jess: Mostly existing customers in ap-southeast1 and ap-northeast1. Two customers attached curl traces and a tcpdump showing repeated SYN->SYN/ACK delays and occasional RSTs.
Sam: I pulled metrics — sharp p99 uplift at 09:08UTC in ap-southeast1 egress nodes. p95 also up. No CPU/GPU spike; throughput steady.
Lee: Any DNS hints? Could be an anycast shift or upstream resolver returning suboptimal paths.
Maria: Support attached sample curl: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` shows TLS handshake ~2400ms before 1st ACK from our side.
Ajay: Post the customer traceroute and edge tcpdump for 09:07-09:12UTC.
Support Jess: Customer traceroute: ```traceroute to api.redwood.ai (35.201.10.5), 12 hops max, 60 byte packets
1 10.30.0.1 0.5 ms 0.4 ms 0.4 ms
2 100.64.0.1 7.1 ms 7.0 ms 7.2 ms
3 203.77.111.20 18.2 ms 18.1 ms 18.3 ms
4 103.21.33.45 120.9 ms 121.0 ms 120.8 ms
5 35.201.10.5 121.7 ms 121.9 ms 121.5 ms``` Note the big jump at hop 4 (120ms).
Sam: That jump suggests a transit handoff or cross-region hairpin. Could explain TLS retransmits and handshake timeouts.
Ops-bot: Alert: ap-southeast1-egress-p95 latency > 1100ms between 09:06-09:14UTC (rolling window 8m).
Lee: I see BGP withdraws/announces from a couple peer ASNs around 09:05-09:06UTC. No planned maintenance logged.
Maria: No deploys at that time. Nets, any scheduled work?
Ajay: Not planned. Hypothesis: upstream ISP rerouted traffic causing a detour to a remote POP, adding cross-AZ/region hops and packet loss leading to long TLS handshakes.
Support Jess: Customers report client-side retries; some SDKs open new connections per request which amplifies the impact.
Lee: Immediate mitigations: 1) advise customers to enable connection pooling/keepalive, 2) steer egress prefix to an alternate transit peer with better latency, 3) if configured, reduce TLS renegotiation aggressiveness on affected POP.
Sam: I'll prepare a routing change request to steer via peer-B (better RTT). Need nets oncall approval.
Maria: Nets oncall @Lee please coordinate. Support: send customers suggested SDK settings and apologies; call out Dedicated vs Hosted tenants.
Lee: Applied manual BGP change to prefer peer-B for ap-southeast1 egress at 09:28UTC. Observability shows p99 dropping gradually; by 09:40UTC p99 largely back to baseline. Continuing to monitor.
Support Jess: Affected customers notified; one enterprise confirmed they'll enable pooling immediately. I've offered credits if SLA affected.
Ajay: Longer-term suggestion: add handshake-setup latency metric and auto-failover when sustained >500ms for 5m so egress can choose alternate peer before customer impact escalates.
Sam: Filed ENG-SRE-620 to add TLS handshake latency instrumentation + alerting.
Lee: Filed NETOPS-482: BGP peer health thresholds + NETOPS-483: auto-eject unhealthy peer.
Maria: Action items: support notify customers (Support Jess), nets confirm routing change window and rollback plan (Lee), eng-sre add handshake metric & alerts (Sam), product to review SDK defaults (Ajay). I'll draft a short postmortem with timeline and included traceroutes.
Ops-bot: Incident closed for ap-southeast1-egress-p95 at 10:05UTC — baseline observed for 30m. Reminder: postmortem due in 72h.
Maria: Thanks all. I'll collate artifacts and schedule a 30m follow-up. :thumbsup:
